# When Both Saves Changed the Same Thing

#### Course: Practical Git and GitHub

## When Both Saves Changed the Same Thing

Sometimes, both branches change the same line. Git cannot decide which version to keep, so it stops and asks you to resolve it.

```python
$ git merge update-nav
```

Output

```text
Auto-merging index.html CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in index.html Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
```

Open index.html. Git has marked the conflicting section:

```python
<<<<<<< HEAD Programiz — Learn to Code
 ======= Programiz — Free Programming Tutorials

 >>>>>>> update-nav
```

Reading the markers:

- <<<<<<< HEAD to ======= — the version on your current branch (main)
- ======= to >>>>>>> — the version coming in from the other branch

Git has not deleted either version. Both are there. You decide which wins.

Edit the file to the version you want — remove the markers, keep the right content:

```python
Programiz — Free Programming Tutorials
```

Then finish the merge:

```python
$ git add index.html 
 $ git commit -m "Merge update-nav: use updated page title"
```

Output

```text
[main 8b2d4f6] Merge update-nav: use updated page title
```

Done. The conflict markers are gone. Both branches' work is now part of main.
